intro.title: Build typed plugin hooks with lifecycle events
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, typed plugin system that uses lifecycle events to manage plugins. You will learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define the structure and expected behavior of a plugin, ensuring type safety. The core concept involves creating a hook manager that can register plugins and trigger specific events, like 'initialize' or 'cleanup', at the right times. You'll work with TypeScript's type system, interfaces, and arrays to handle plugin operations. By the end, you'll have a functional system where plugins can be added and their lifecycle methods called in a type-safe way.
intro.usecase: Typed plugin hooks with lifecycle events are essential in enterprise applications like content management systems, e-commerce platforms, and developer tools. For example, in a dashboard builder like WordPress or Shopify, plugins need to initialize data when loaded, respond to user interactions in admin panels, and clean up resources when disabled. This pattern ensures plugins integrate safely with core systems—validating data on form submissions, managing state in analytics widgets, and handling cleanup in modal workflows. As a developer, you'll implement these hooks to create extensible, maintainable plugins that follow predictable lifecycle patterns.
